text_blocks.snippet: Choosing between a metal roof and asphalt shingles in Utah depends on balancing a higher initial investment against long-term durability in heavy snow, high winds, and intense UV rays. Asphalt roofs cost $10,000 to $18,000 and last 20 to 30 years, while metal roofs cost $20,000 to $40,000+ and last 40 to 70 years.

text_blocks.snippet: To help you decide which material fits your mountain or valley home, here is how they compare across key factors.
Watch this video for a detailed visual comparison of the durability and design differences between metal and shingle roofs:

list.snippet: Asphalt Shingles: Lower upfront cost. Architectural shingles last roughly 20–30 years. You will likely replace an asphalt roof two times in the span of one long-lasting metal roof.
Metal Roof: Higher initial price tag (often 2 to 3 times more expensive than shingles), but functions as a "one-and-done" long-term investment that rarely needs replacement.

Snow & Ice: Metal roofs excel in heavy snow zones (like Park City, Wasatch Back, or mountain benches) because smooth panels allow snow to slide off safely rather than accumulating and straining the structure. Asphalt traps more snow and ice, risking ice dams during freeze-thaw cycles.

Wind & Sun: High-quality installations of both handle standard Utah winds well, though metal resists extreme UV degradation and high winds better over decades. Asphalt granules can loosen and wash away under intense high-altitude UV exposure.

HOA Rules: Asphalt shingles are universally accepted by neighborhood HOAs. Metal roofing styles (especially exposed fastener panels) may face restrictions or require specific standing-seam aesthetics in suburban developments.

Repairs: Shingle damage from localized issues or minor storms is fast, cheap, and easy to repair. Metal repairs are less frequent, but if a panel is severely dented or damaged by heavy impact, replacing the section is more complex.
